blocks.text: EXAMPLE COUNTY FIRE CHIEFS ASSOCIATION
WATER SUPPLY STANDARD OPERATING GUIDELINE
Adopted March 2024
PURPOSE
This guideline establishes how member agencies establish and sustain water supply at working structure fires under the automatic aid agreement.
PROCEDURE
A. The first arriving engine company shall secure its own supply before committing to fire attack, except where an officer determines that a rescue takes precedence.
B. The second arriving engine company shall establish a supply line from the nearest hydrant capable of delivering the required flow.
C. Supply responsibilities are assigned as follows.
1. Water Supply Officer - The third arriving company officer shall assume the Water Supply assignment and report the established flow to Command.
2. Hydrant Assignment - Companies shall not draft from a hydrant already supplying an aerial apparatus without the approval of the Water Supply Officer.
EXAMPLE COUNTY SOG - WATER SUPPLY
Page 2 of 2
3. Relay Operations - Where hydrant spacing exceeds the distance a single company can supply, relay pumping shall be established under the following conditions.
a. The supplying company shall confirm the discharge pressure with the receiving company before charging the line.
b. Intake pressure shall not be allowed to fall below twenty pounds per square inch at any point in the relay.
c. The Water Supply Officer shall confirm the following before the relay is placed in service.
i. The total length of hose in the relay and the elevation change across it.
ii. The rated capacity of every pump operating in the relay.
iii. The identity of the officer responsible for each pump position.
d. A relay shall not be shut down without notifying every company operating from it.
D. Any member may report a water supply problem directly to Command without going through the Water Supply Officer.
